concerns.concern: All edge spectra and the map lie within about ±100 mV of E_F, right at the valence-band edge, not across the claimed ~300 meV gap. An edge enhancement at the band edge is equally compatible with trivial edge, band-bending or Fermi-level-pinned states, and no mid-gap edge-versus-center comparison is shown.
concerns.quote: No edge vs center comparison is shown at mid-gap energies (e.g. 100–250 meV). This is the key test.

concerns.concern: The measured 390 pm Si2Te2 lattice constant conflicts with the claimed 1×1 hollow-site registry on HfTe2 (~395–397 pm). A commensurate layer would be strained, and an unstrained layer would form a moiré. The line-profile measurement cannot resolve the difference, and no in-situ lattice ratio is reported.
concerns.quote: If HfTe2 has a ≈ 395–397 pm, these two claims are hard to reconcile.

concerns.concern: The 'strain-free' DFT result is forced by the commensurate 1×1 supercell, which makes both layers share one lattice constant. The HfTe2 lattice constant is never reported, and the strain absorbed by the monolayer HfTe2 is neglected. This affects the binding energy and the band alignment.
concerns.quote: 'Strain-free' DFT result is largely imposed by the commensurate 1×1 supercell

concerns.concern: The edge signal is a sharp dI/dV peak, but a linearly dispersing 1D mode should give a flat, plateau-like LDOS enhancement across the gap. The justification is deferred entirely to the supplemental material.
concerns.quote: A sharp peak instead points to a flat-band, van Hove or localized-state contribution.

concerns.concern: The dI/dV map is taken at a single energy in constant-current mode, so the setpoint effect at island edges could create an apparent edge ring. There are no contrasting maps at other energies, and the missing signal along part of the edge is blamed on tip effects without evidence.
concerns.quote: This setpoint effect can produce an apparent edge ring independent of any edge state.

concerns.concern: Claiming the 'first experimental realization of the QSH phase' overstates LDOS-only evidence. Band inversion is not probed, there is no transport or spin measurement, and the metallic substrate shunts any edge conduction.
concerns.quote: 'realization of the QSH phase' overstates what STS can establish

concerns.concern: The predicted 319 meV 'experimental gap' is built by subtracting the ML-HfTe2 VBM offset, even though HfTe2 is a semimetal with states at E_F. The agreement with the measured ~300 meV gap therefore rests on an ad hoc construction using a monolayer rather than the actual bulk substrate.
concerns.quote: This agreement depends on an ad hoc construction based on ML-HfTe2, which is not the actual (bulk) substrate.

concerns.concern: The 0.25 eV DFT–STS offset is blamed on substrate doping that DFT misses, but the substrate is explicitly in the model. The model actually predicts the opposite doping (E_F below the VBM), so the discrepancy needs a specific, testable cause.
concerns.quote: the discrepancy therefore lies in the sign or magnitude of the doping predicted by the model. It is not a missing effect.

concerns.concern: The edge-state calculation geometry is underspecified: it is unclear whether HfTe2 is included, which edge termination is used, and how metallic substrate states and hybridization are handled. These choices determine whether the calculation is relevant to the measured geometry.
concerns.quote: These choices determine whether Fig. 2(b) is relevant to the measurement.

concerns.concern: The sign convention of the lattice-mismatch window appears inverted relative to the −3% to +2% strain tolerance. The broadened window then extends toward the less tolerant tensile side, which could change which candidates pass the screening.
concerns.quote: the filter is asymmetric in the wrong direction. This could change which candidates pass.

concerns.concern: The claimed substrate-induced gap enhancement from 220 to 429 meV may simply reflect comparing different functionals (e.g. PBE vs HSE06). If both are HSE06, the large shift instead suggests strain or charge transfer. A same-method free-standing comparison is needed.
concerns.quote: Large substrate-induced gap enhancement (220 → 429 meV) needs a same-method comparison

concerns.concern: The edge-state width is quoted inconsistently (≈2 nm and 2–3 nm), and calling it 'good agreement' with a DFT value of 1.35 nm is overstated. The DFT value also comes from free-standing ribbons, and the width definition is not given.
concerns.quote: we estimate the edge-state width to be ≈2 nm

concerns.concern: The low-bias minimum at the island center is described as ±50 mV in one figure and ±10 mV in another. Neither matches the ~300 meV bulk gap, so its origin is unclear even though it serves as the reference for judging the edge peak.
concerns.quote: The center spectrum exhibits a V-shaped dip between ±50 mV

concerns.concern: The measured 710 pm step height differs by ~11% from the calculated 790 pm spacing. The planes defining the 790 pm are not specified, and the bias dependence of STM apparent heights is not considered.
concerns.quote: is in reasonable agreement with the calculated interlayer spacing

concerns.concern: The screening count of candidates passing the lattice-mismatch filter is 76 in the text but 65 in Fig. 1(a), which makes the screening statistics unverifiable as written.

The growth recipe is underspecified: absolute Si and Te fluxes, the flux ratio, deposition time, coverage and annealing duration are missing, and the final growth temperature is ambiguous (385 °C called optimal while coverage loss starts above 320 °C).
concerns.quote: 'Exceeding 20 times the nominal rate' is not reproducible without the nominal rate.

concerns.concern: The Z2/WCC method is cited to an unrelated reference instead of the standard sources (Soluyanov & Vanderbilt; Yu et al.), and the code used is not named.
concerns.quote: calculating the Z2 invariant via the evolution of Wannier charge centers (WCCs) [39]

concerns.concern: The description of the supplemental material mentions stripe orientations that appear nowhere in this paper and seems to be carried over from another manuscript.
concerns.quote: large area scans showing the coexistence of three stripe orientations
